Folks who argue that the moon landings are real often cite the retroreflectors left by the astronauts (special mirrors we can shine lasers on to measure the return) as proof that man walked on the moon.

I say: the retroreflectors do *not* prove that man walked on the moon, since three of the five active retroreflectors were placed by unmanned Soviet landers, and in fact the primary one used for lunar science today was placed by an unmanned lander.

There is so much sloppiness in critical thinking online that it drives me up the wall, and this is one of my favorite examples. So many "lists of things that prove man walked on the moon" list the retroreflectors, and I've seen them offered a few times as "booya!" level debate-winners on the issue.

There are a number of problems with the retroreflectors in general, but more than anything they don't prove that man visited the moon because, as I said - most of them are there on unmanned probes.

Now here is where so many folks really seem to lose the plot:

This does not "prove" that man did not visit the moon. No way in hell. There's still a mountain of evidence showing that twelve individuals bounced around in 1/6 gravity in the 60s and 70s. The only reason I ever bring it up is because it's not evidence. Not that it's "weak" evidence - but that it's not evidence whatsoever. So stop trying to use it to prove people walked on the moon. You can kind of use it to show that we have placed probes on the moon (though even that is a stretch), but I really don't think that's what folks are trying to prove.

I think the problem is that people who believe that man walked on the moon have fixated this image of an astronaut placing a retroreflector in their head, so to them proving the retroreflector is up there "proves" that a man must have put it there - that's the first failure in critical thinking.

And the second failure is believing that an attack on one piece of evidence is an attack on the underlying hypothesis, which is an easy mistake to make, but a critical failure in debate.

I watched the moon landing on TV, and I followed the space program the whole time I was growing up. I have zero doubt that the Apollo astronauts landed on the moon. But that doesn't mean I'm happy to see sloppy thinking in debating the point. ;-)
